newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Middle-of-night shelling rocks Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: Middle-of-night shelling rocks Brazzaville.

text.p: A mystery burst of shellfire rocked the Congolese capital Brazzaville in the small hours of Monday, dying away before first light on day three of a new ceasefire.

"It woke me up at about three o'clock. We've got no idea who was firing. I did see some tracer fire but I've got no idea where it came from," one expatriate still in the capital told Reuters by telephone.
The sound of nighttime explosions from Brazzaville could also be heard across the Congo river in Kinshasa, the capital of Laurent Kabila's "other" Congo, formerly Zaire.
The rest of the morning was calm, residents said.
Despite some gunfire, Sunday was one of Brazzaville's calmest days in a bloody civil war that started on June 5 but a lasting solution seems no nearer.
The city has been devastated and many hundreds of its residents killed in the conflict between President Pascal Lissouba and former military leader Denis Sassou Nguess.
Both say they want free and fair presidential elections, planned for late July, to proceed as soon as possible but disagree on how they should be organised.
